Subject: Request to purge historical prompts/outputs and invocation logs (SyncHealth account)

Hi Irene,

Per our retention policy review, SyncHealth needs Redwood to expunge all user prompt text, generated outputs, and per-invocation logs tied to the environment id SH-44321 for the period Jan 1 2026 - Mar 31 2027. This includes:
- raw prompts and prompt metadata (not aggregated metrics)
- generated output artifacts (text and attachments)
- request/response invocation logs (timestamps, token counts, model id)

Can you confirm the steps you will take, an estimated completion window, and an audit artifact we can consume once the sweep is complete? We need evidence for our security team (SOC items).

Alex — thank you for the clear scope. We can run a targeted retention sweep for environment SH-44321. High level plan: 
1) Identify records by environment id + timestamp range (Jan 1 2026 - Mar 31 2027).
2) Execute tiered purge: prompt bodies -> generated outputs -> invocation logs. Logs are sharded; we will remove PII-linked fields and then tombstone invocation rows as required.
3) Run verification queries and produce a CSV of deleted identifiers plus an audit PDF summarizing the steps and hashes of artifacts.

Rishi (ops) / Monica (legal) — can you confirm estimated ETA and whether we need a Data Processing Addendum amendment before executing?

Irene Choi

Irene — operational note: for SH-44321 the data spans three storage classes (fast-ssd KV cache, cold object store, and aggregated telemetry DB). Estimated timeline if we run weekday job windows: 48-72 hours for full sweep, verification included. Steps:
- Day 0: quarantine snapshot + start deletion jobs (non-blocking reads preserved until tombstone).
- Day 1: purge prompts and outputs from KV and object store.
- Day 2: purge invocation rows and run integrity checks.

I'll schedule a canary on ~50K rows first and share execution CSV. We will produce a retention-sweep-execution.csv with deleted record ids and timestamps, and an audit-evidence-stub.pdf with hashes. No additional DPA amendment required for this scoped request — Monica, please confirm.
